title: City land framework and advisory committee honoraria
subtitle: Donating old computers, emergency by-law, traffic signs, a zoning hold removal and committee terms of reference
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended a framework to guide how surplus City-owned land is managed and sold. Staff would treat the land as one portfolio and focus on affordable housing and the Make a Kitchener investment fund. Staff would also bring options to Council for decision later {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended that end-of-life City laptops and desktops go to local community groups and The Working Centre's computer recycling program instead of e-waste. It also asked that the resolution be shared with the Region and other local municipalities {{vote:m7}}.

On committee honoraria, the committee recommended a policy that sets honoraria and reimbursements for advisory and quasi-judicial committees. It asked staff to develop a separate approach for the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee, and to update the terms of reference for Property Standards and Committee of Adjustment {{vote:m8}}. A staff clause on honoraria for public engagement was removed from consideration.

Routine items covered an updated emergency management by-law, new traffic signs and parking limits, re-appointments to the accessibility committee and lifting a zoning holding provision at 1950 Fischer Hallman Road. A strategic plan update was received for information. All of these recommendations go to Council for final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council adopt the framework, direct staff to manage surplus City land as an asset portfolio, and have staff bring disposition and acquisition options to Council.

The committee recommended redirecting end-of-life laptops and desktops from e-waste to community groups and The Working Centre, continuing donations to non-profits, and circulating the resolution to the Region and local municipalities.

The committee recommended the policy for advisory and quasi-judicial committees, effective January 2024, a separate approach for the accessibility committee, and updated terms of reference for Property Standards and Committee of Adjustment.
The committee recommended that Council approve the revised Terms of Reference for the Downtown Advisory Committee.
The committee recommended that Council approve the updated Emergency Management By-law.
The committee recommended new stop signs on Tecumseh Crescent and Lynnvalley Crescent, removal of an existing stop control on Lynnvalley Court, and a parking prohibition on part of Joshua Street.
The committee recommended removing Holding Provision 67H from the lands at 1950 Fischer Hallman Road.

The committee recommended re-appointing three Kitchener members to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for a term ending December 31, 2027, pending ratification by partner municipalities.

debate: On land disposition, councillors asked how downtown parking would be balanced and whether long-term leases could be used instead of sales. Staff said each parcel would be assessed for need and that leases are an option in the framework.

Councillors asked about neighbouring-land assembly, upzoning and the small leftover parcels the City owns. One suggested a reminder in the policy not to empty the supply of land for future councils, and staff said that would fit the intent.

On computers, councillors asked to promote the program to community centres, seniors, schools, newcomer groups and cultural associations. A Working Centre representative said prices run from $30 to $250 to recover costs, and staff said the Windows reinstall takes about two hours.

On honoraria, some councillors said advisory committee members' work deserved pay and that cost should not stop people taking part. Others worried about paying volunteers and about costs growing, and wanted to avoid a staff-heavy receipt process for small amounts. Staff said honoraria are not meant to replace volunteerism and that reimbursement tackles barriers like travel and childcare.

Councillors discussed whether the third staff clause, on honoraria and reimbursement for public engagement, should be voted on. Staff said they would continue to look at barriers to participation, and the clause was struck without a vote.
